To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a local entity-based model can be effective even when estimated generatively, and (2) local and global models can be learned jointly, and the global model is useful even when the local model is not.

we present a model for coherence which combines a local entity-based approach with a global content model, and that we adapt the local model to allow for dependencies between entities, which makes it effective when estimated generativelv.

we present a unified local and global model for discourse coherence that is based on the entity-based model of (Barazilay and Lapta, 2005), and the HMM model of (Barilay and Lee. 2004), and is more competitive than (Soricutand Marcu, 206), the current best model, and the entity-based model and the HMM on their own.

developing a unified local and global discourse coherence model which can be used for ordering, and is effective in both the local and global settings.
the problem of discourse coherence and the development of models which can be used to predict the coherence of sentences and document segments.
developing a model of discourse coherence that is theoretically motivated, computationally efficient and competitive with current state-of-the-art systems.
